pillar_reactions.evidence: The philosophy presentation never ran. The call went from discovery directly to the price at 00:12:23 and then to withdrawal, so none of the three pillars were delivered. The prospect had asked twice what the programme actually is — 'I wasn't sure if this would lead to get a specific program, like a workout schedule from kettlebells or not' — and left without being told.

The conflict was never surfaced because the pillar was never presented.

anchors.raw: I've been doing quite a bunch of, I'd say Trevor's workouts, you know, from Instagram saving a bunch. A lot of them seem to be really good, that I enjoy doing.
anchors.note: He is already getting what he wants from the free material, and the rep actively reinforced the anchor rather than reframing it: 'go through Trevor's workouts, keep going through them, do it for like a month' and 'there's loads of stuff on YouTube, loads of education from Trevor on YouTube, go through it, get stuck in there.' Defensible as a disqualification, but it leaves the prospect with a strengthened belief that the free tier is sufficient.

anchors.raw: I worked with a personal trainer over, let's say the last two months and kind of the same outcome, right? I really kind of built up and it's really not what I was trying to achieve.
anchors.competitor: his personal trainer and his nutritionist
anchors.note: He already pays for both a personal trainer and a nutritionist who has run blood analysis, so paying for expert guidance is established — but the recent trainer produced the opposite of the outcome he wanted, which lowers rather than raises willingness to pay for the next one. That failed experience is also the origin of his hidden-agenda objection, and neither the trainer's price nor what he got for it was ever established.

unmet_demand.want: Independent validation that a kettlebell routine is sufficient on its own — 'to build a kettlebell kind of routine that works for my life and that has the validation that, okay, that's enough, you don't need to supplement it with anything, from a real trainer'
unmet_demand.why_unmet: What he described is a one-off programme review and sign-off from someone with no incentive to sell him more. The offer is a six-month tailored coaching relationship at $6,000, and the only other thing available is a self-guided community. There is nothing between free content and a six-month commitment, and nothing at all that sells the specific reassurance he asked for. He stated the demand plainly and it was never addressed.

unmet_demand.want: Fat loss for someone who hypertrophies rapidly on any stimulus, with a below-average metabolic rate and elevated cortisol confirmed by blood work
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The programme's nutrition protocol leans on fasting, which his nutritionist has specifically told him to stop because it raises his morning cortisol. Whether the approach can be adapted for that, and how a training method sold on building muscle serves someone whose complaint is building too much of it, was never discussed. The rep's only response to the hypertrophy problem was 'you're like the only guy I've ever heard who's like, oh, I'm getting too big too quick.'
